prose_updates.tldr: For scalar rank-one squared-contrast transport with any fixed number \(K\) of empirical marginals and fixed coefficient vector \(\widetilde c\), the same-\(N\) realization loss has an exact support-size phase transition: it is zero when at most two coefficients are nonzero and is \(\Theta_{\widetilde c}(N^{-1})\) when at least three are nonzero.  Ordered dual-slope roots of lengths \(H_j=2\|\widetilde c\|_1-|\widetilde c_j|\), active-arm basic-table freezing, and hierarchical repair give the explicit upper constant \((16r^2/3)\sum_jH_j^2\), while affine placement of the padded four-row obstruction gives \(5\lambda_{\widetilde c}^2/N\) on every \(N\ge4\).  For the causal contrast \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\), the upper constant is exactly \(402\) and the transferred lower constant improves incidentally to \(5/215296\).  The complete-randomization application remains the original three-arm finite-population variance certificate, whose deterministic realization width is \(O(N^{-2})\); sampling-without-replacement uncertainty remains separate and larger.

project_justification.gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) identify superpopulation causal variance bounds over fractional multi-marginal couplings, whereas a fixed population of \(N\) units requires one common \(N\)-row schedule; the distinction is operational and does not contradict their theorem.  Existing non-Monge, mixability, and integer-programming results do not determine how this same-denominator loss changes with the support size of a fixed scalar contrast.
project_justification.niche: The mathematical object is the fractional-versus-realizable loss for \(K\) scalar \([0,1]\) empirical marginals under one fixed rank-one squared contrast.  The general theorem varies \(K\) only at the transport layer; the causal design, estimand, endpoint functional, and empirical application remain the original three-arm contrast.  Arbitrary vector-valued outcome dimension \(d\) and a general quadratic matrix \(A\) are outside the achievability theorem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves integrality for zero, one, or two active coefficients; for \(r\ge3\) it gives the deterministic bound \(\Delta_{N,K,\widetilde c}<(16r^2/3N)\sum_jH_j^2\), a polynomial exact-rational repair algorithm, and the matching all-\(N\ge4\) affine lower family \(5\lambda_{\widetilde c}^2/N\).  It then specializes exactly to the \(402/N\) three-arm guarantee and retains the design-based variance and plug-in certificates.

prose_updates.related_work: Emami and Pass (2025, Introduction, Example 1, and Discussion) move from the empirical Kantorovich relaxation to Monge implementability, prove a minimal non-Monge quadratic example, and identify quantitative approximation error as future work; their barycenter cost has the opposite squared-sum orientation from the signed scalar contrast here.  Friesecke (2019, Theorem 2.2 and Section 3) analyzes non-Monge extreme points in a symmetric finite transport polytope but gives no all-denominator additive rate.  Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) identify a superpopulation causal bound with fractional multi-marginal transport and prove plug-in rates; Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}variance\mbox{-}certificate}\) instead quantifies the operational error incurred when the same empirical marginals must be realized by one fixed-population schedule.  Haus (2015) studies exact matrix mixability and bottleneck approximation, while Altschuler and Boix-Adser\`a (2023) restore exact marginals inside the fractional transportation polytope.  Puccetti and Wang (2015) give rearrangement representations and higher-dimensional dependence geometry, but their discretization comparison changes marginals rather than imposing same-\(N\) realizability.  Brennan et al. (2025) compute broad finite causal completions by integer programming.  The new transport theorem identifies a support-size dichotomy for every fixed scalar coefficient vector: two active marginals are integral, while three or more have matching \(N^{-1}\) upper and lower rates.  This does not extend the achievability claim to arbitrary outcome dimension \(d\) or a general quadratic form \(A\).  Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014) remain the exact two-arm causal comparator; Li and Ding (2017) supply the fixed-potential-outcome randomization framework, and Hammer et al. (1996) provide the multi-arm trial consumer.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The coefficient-dependent upper constant \((16r^2/3)\sum_jH_j^2\) is universal but deliberately conservative and can grow rapidly with the active support size.  Even at the original contrast, \(402/N\) improves on the trivial \(1/4\) cost-gap bound only at \(N=1609\), so ordinary-size trials should report the actual primal--dual width.  The exact normalized constant and extremal geometry remain open; the new affine transfer only improves the original lower localization to \(5/215296\) for the fixed three-arm contrast.  Plug-in sampling error dominates deterministic rounding error under proportional allocation.  The proof uses scalar ordering and rank-one squared-sum algebra and does not establish achievability for arbitrary vector dimension \(d\) or a general quadratic matrix \(A\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note proves the complete support-size dichotomy for every fixed scalar rank-one contrast: exact zero loss for at most two active arms and \(\Theta_{\widetilde c}(N^{-1})\) for at least three, with explicit coefficient-dependent constants, an all-\(N\ge4\) lower family, and an exact-rational polynomial construction for fixed \(K\).  Its causal claim remains narrower: the finite-population variance translation and plug-in analysis concern complete randomization with the original three arms and \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\).  The result is an operational same-science-table correction to a fractional functional, not a contradiction of a superpopulation identified-set theorem.  It does not claim that one experiment observes all full marginals, that every interior variance is attainable, that the unknown actual completion has variance at least \(U_{\mathrm{lo}}(F)\), or that the upper construction covers arbitrary \(d\) and general quadratic \(A\).  The exact value of \(\Delta_3\) and the limit of \(N\Delta_N\) remain outside the proved result; the two-row realization loss for the original contrast is exactly zero.
